title: Fit kernel ridge regression and approximate it with random features
brief: Solve (K + lambda I) alpha = y with a Cholesky factor, match that prediction to the Gaussian-process posterior mean, then replace the kernel with random Fourier features.
hints: kernel_ridge_fit needs K + lam * np.eye(n) on the diagonal only. Factor it with np.linalg.cholesky to get a triangular L, then solve L z = y and L^T alpha = z. Do not form an inverse.
kernel_ridge_predict is one matrix-vector product, K_test @ alpha, where K_test has one row per query and one column per training point.
implied_weights is X.T @ alpha. For a linear kernel K = X X^T it equals the weights of ordinary ridge regression, (X^T X + lam I)^{-1} X^T y.
representer_check evaluates one formula: the summed squared error on the first len(y) entries of K @ coeffs, plus lam * coeffs @ K @ coeffs. It works for any list of centres K was built from.

For random_fourier_features, draw omega with shape (D, d) from a normal distribution scaled by sqrt(2 * gamma), then D phases uniform on [0, 2 pi). Test points must reuse the same draw, so take all randomness from the rng you are given.
ridge_on_features solves the D by D system (Z^T Z + lam I) w = Z^T y. Use np.linalg.solve; it needs no inverse.

gp_posterior_mean is kernel ridge with lam set to the noise variance: kernel_ridge_fit(K, y, noise), then kernel_ridge_predict. Add noise on the diagonal of K, not as a multiplier of K. The variance at a query is prior_var + noise minus k dotted with the solution of (K + noise I) z = k.
